label: Surface pattern
description: Named textile and surface motifs: checks, stripes, florals, geometrics, animal prints and resist-dyed designs.
notes: Named motifs and visible surface arrangements belong here, phrased as adjectives or noun-adjuncts before fabric. clothing.fabric owns the underlying cloth and its physical texture; object.material owns nontextile substances. Regional names identify recognizable designs without implying the wearer’s descent or restricting where a motif can appear. Checks and stripes are specific constructions rather than generic duplicates, and the historical William Morris reference describes a dense botanical pattern rather than a fabric brand.
